newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU justice chief wants to stop forced prostitution.
newsitem.headline: EU justice chief wants to stop forced prostitution.

text.p: EU Justice Commissioner Anita Gradin said on Friday that legalising prostitution was not necessary in order to clamp down on the illegal trafficking of women for sex.

Gradin, who is leading the European Union's efforts to end the illegal trade in sex, said she was surprised by a leading European Parliament deputy's remark that her goal could not be achieved without legalising voluntary prostitution.

"I don't understand that you have to link the question of legalising prostitution with trafficking in women because in most cases prostitution is legal," Gradin told Reuters. "In most countries it's not prostitution that's criminalised, its those that are using it," she said.

She is seeking an EU-wide solution to the problem of women tempted from eastern Europe by the promise of a better life in the West as dancers, hostesses and hairdressers, only to be forced into prostitution on arrival.

Euro-MP Nel van Dijk, chairwoman of the Women's Rights Committee, told Reuters in a recent interview that it was "important to ensure the criminal part of prostitution is abolished and brought under control".
But there was no need to stamp out prostitution altogether, she added. "Why would you want to?" she asked.
Gradin, the Swede who put the issue on the EU's agenda at a major conference in Vienna last year, said she could not understand why the two issues should be linked.
Van Dijk said Gradin's approach was too narrow. "The Commissioner does not accept calling prostitution work..." she said.

Adopting such a "moral and clean hands approach" had the effect of sweeping all prostitution under the carpet, ruling out any legal control over the business and giving more power to the illegal pimps, she said.

Van Dijk said women in legal brothels in Amsterdam earned good wages, paid taxes, got social security and could leave when they liked, while illegal prostitutes were trapped in the clutches of often violent pimps because they had no identity papers or wages.
